Overview

The economics of Agentic AI & Hyperautomation for Banking & Financial Services flipped in the last two years: runtimes got durable, evaluation became routine, and orchestration frameworks matured into something you can run under change control. What separates winners now is integration discipline — how cleanly the capability plugs into core banking rails without inventing a shadow estate. What makes Banking & Financial Services different is not the math; it is the operating context: DORA operational resilience governs the data, instant rails governs the economics, and the people accountable for outcomes answer to regulators as well as customers. Every design choice below is downstream of that context.

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship
The ways programs like this die — and the guard we ship against each:

items: Duplicated work
Duplicated work: blackboard contracts make task claims exclusive, so two agents can never own the same case; the guard is part of the first slice, not a hardening phase
Runaway loops
Runaway loops — durable execution caps retries, tool calls and spend per run; breach trips a kill switch that pages the owner
Agent sprawl
Agent sprawl — every agent ships with a role spec, budget and owner — unregistered agents are quarantined at the queue
